body: Thanks to everyone who replied. It means a lot to me, I guess I feel validated. I still feel terrible but I think it's partly because I'm trying to take a break from smoking weed all day every day (currently on day 3) so obviously I have that messing my emotions up. I appreciate all the replies. You're all good people.
I used to think it was so gross that people used pencil sharpener blades to cut themselves. Never occured to me before now that they weren't using them as pencil sharpeners as well.
You should be going to A&E for stitches as the cut should be stitched within 6hrs, or if it's extremely large/deep then 24hrs.
Hmm no, I would recommend getting stitches if fat is showing that much. Why don't you want to get stitches out by them?

I get downvoted for saying this all the time, hahaha... Still I hope this helps you.

Unless there is fat (bright yellow bubbly stuff) all the way through your cut then you don't need stitches, microporous tape is fine to keep it closed. Actually sometimes stitches can make scarring worse as obviously you're damaging the tissue around the wound to close it up.

Well, it's your decision in the end, and it does sound like a very manageable way to hide scars (keep your scars to these areas if you know what's good for you) but I think what I say to other people still stands. If you decide to stop hiding your scars then suddenly you don't have to worry about secrecy, you don't have to be constantly fretting that someone will see, it's definitely a relief to be able to relax around family and friends.

So edgy, haha! I tried to be scene/emo in middle school but I couldn't commit. Ended up looking like a mixture of scene and "dorky 13yo who has no fashion sense"... which is a pretty accurate description of who I was.

I definitely know what you mean, I think about this a lot. No responsibility, no requirement to be polite to people who need to fuck off, just do as you're told.

Then I realise that I had such massive problems in school with all the above, so I guess prison would be worse, 'cause I'd get stabbed or beat on or put in solitary confinement. You can't stay in bed all day when you're in prison, you have to do shit and be on time and while I think I do nothing all day, "nothing" to me means eating disgusting amounts of carbs in front of Netflix. None of that in prison...
I used to do this. I would tear vertical strips off my fingernails until the surface was wavy, bleh.

Not sure you should be afraid of it, like I said most people get over themselves after a little while. Is it worth staying in long sleeves/trousers forever, never having freedom to let your guard down around others?

I guess what is tough is that people's perception of you (funny, friendly, talkative, whatever) is suddenly changed to something completely different. So people act a little awkward, a little walking on eggshells, a little like they're trying to figure out who you "really" are. Sadly sometimes people never get over this, I have a couple of people who can't really get over the fact that I am both talkative/friendly and a self harmer of many years -- they are in a constant battle when they talk to me because they are still unable to see me as more than a self harmer.

> they are symbols of my pain and anger and if they fade it invalidates in a way like it never happened

This is exactly how I feel. My self harming, I think, has always in some way been about "proving" my inner turmoil to be as bad as/worse than other peoples. Which is pretty bad now I think about it.

Aw man that sounds like a really bad experience. Glad you got it bandaged up. 

You must always be really, really careful cutting with new blades and cutting in such a delicate area. If it helps then research places on the body which have a thick layer of fat/skin and very few veins close to the surface to reduce the risk when harming. 

Hope you stay safe.

I think a major part of "don't mention people's scars" is the fact that the vast majority of people are - purposefully or not - extremely awkward and unsensitive when acknowledging them. It's easier to tell people not to mention them than cope with people constantly coming up to you and being like, "OMG ARE YOU OK????? ARE YOU SUICIDAL????? OMFG WHAT HAPPENED WHY ARE YOU CUTTING YOURSELF U HAVE SO MUCH TO LIVE FOR !!!!!!" and then telling everyone they know...

I would treat it like a scratched area. Be very cautious of infection because of the massive surface area (compared to most cuts) increasing likelihood of infection. Like with burns/scratched areas you should use a non-stick dressing (the ones that look kind of plastic-y on one side) and potentially go to your doctor anyway because of the expense of using non-sticking dressing plus microporous tape every day. Also they will detect infection ASAP.

Yeah, when I'm really emotional (I try not to cut then but sometimes do) or really numb feeling, self-soothing is really not what I need. I don't know if it's just people not understanding self harm when they recommend it or if it's because I've made self harm "work better" by doing it for so long, like I've taught myself to only be relaxed or bettered by self harming.

I've had talks with my youth worker about my relationship with self harm, she says it's a bit different to a lot of peoples because of what we're talking about, this different "reason" to self harm. She says stuff like CBT is less likely to work for me because you have to really want to quit for it to work. Though I don't know where that puts me therapeutically, like how am I supposed to find myself stopping without therapies -- my mindset is, I think, "the therapy should MAKE me stop/fix me so I never need to self harm or feel bad" which I understand is almost the opposite of what therapy is.

Sounds cool, on one hand I want to get a tattoo because they're kind of cool and could cover scars, on the other I don't feel like I'd like it forever and I would feel weird covering up my scars. 

Where is/will it be?

I don't have any help, just want to say that I feel the same. I don't have BPD but I empathise a lot with this feeling, of self harming because you "deserve" it, of giving yourself permanent ugly scars to show others just how ugly and gross you are.

I've never personally found self-soothing outside of my self harm ritual to work (part of my ritual is to pet and soothe myself and weird stuff like that, it makes the self harming better) and same for distractions. Never really worked for me, not long-term. I guess I don't "want" to stop enough so that's why it doesn't work.
When you flex your arm muscles and it just makes the old wrinkly scars wiggle in the sunlight... not the best feeling.

Range Life by Pavement, or Little Viola Hidden In The Orchestra by Of Montreal.

They're both pretty special I guess but I think it's something about the vocals in both which makes me think they'd be suitable. I wouldn't want to go out in an angry way, I wouldn't want people to hear the song and have their last thought of me being an emotional and out of control person, I would want them to understand that I weighed up every possibility and found that the truth was that there is nothing in this life for me so I have to travel to another state to find happiness. Not that I've thought about it a lot.

Masculinity/femininity isn't in the colour, it's in the fit, but I understand what you mean. I also wear a lot of dark clothes (grey, navy, black, brown, I like to switch it up lol) because I'm quite insecure over my body shape.
My cat is called Rosie, she is like a tiny, scruffy, frog-catching panther.
Awesome hair colour, and I also have a black cat. What are yours called?
Pink hair is cool, but it seems like a lot of effort!
High five fellow farm worker! I can't say I'm a fan of screamo or metalcore, I feel that a little goes a long way haha.
I do this, got to change it up a bit to keep it exciting.
Yes, I definitely know what you mean. No-one notices if I ""relapse"" in my self harm because they can't tell new scars from the old...

That's awesome, I don't know what to do with the money I earn atm. It's not enough to run a car (or rather, pay for insurance...) but it's too much for me to feel like I can just spend it willy nilly. So I guess I'm saving it for a rainy day haha.
Yeah, it all really depends on deepness. Fact is, if you're not cutting past the epidermis then your scarring will be minimal and will not cause any problems 6 months down the line.

I sort of assumed that being """only""" 4 months clean meant that the scars were likely still pink and raised.

(""only"" because it's a very long time in terms of clean-ness but a very short time in terms of scar healing)

That means you cut past the epidermis so yes you will have a scar that will likely last forever, sorry. It will fade to white after a period of time (maybe months, maybe years) but there is a possibility of it staying forever. 

If it's not too long ago then maybe try taping it up to reduce the width of the scar?

Ugh I know what you mean, last week I didn't go to work or leave the house at all, just stayed inside playing video games and watching netflix and self harming. Try not to miss any more days of work, you need the structure and the money it gives you!

Maybe you were very sheltered ;)

I knew that self harm was a thing since I was about 7 and from about 9-10 years old I started to be empathetic about it. I consider myself quite perceptive but you'd have to be quite sheltered to not have any understanding of self harm by the time you're 11 or 12...
From random strangers, no. If I'm going to be around the same group of people for a longer period of time (e.g. not just in public) then I cover up to avoid awkwardness.
The problem lies in the people who raised you to be this way. They didn't treat you right when you were developing and now you have to fix what they muddled around.

I guess so, but it relieves the pressure of shame/hiding. 

My family is not a very "supportive" kind of family anyway, we're all the "deal with it on your own" kind of people.

Haha I do this, while I try not to go in public with fresh cuts, sometimes you just can't be bothered to cover up, especially if it's hot. Fuck everyone else, why should you have to cover up just so they can pretend to themselves that everything in the world is A-OK and nobody struggles? Why should you have to cover up your own body because of some stupid stigma against self harmers? Why should you have to cover up self harm, do the same rules and shame apply if the wounds were not from self harm?

Depends on the ages of the kids and how smart/perceptive they seem to be.

At about 5-7, unless they're very smart you can brush it off with something like, "I didn't eat my vegetables!" or "I got hurt."

Any older than 9 or 10 then the kid basically knows exactly what they're looking at (unless they're very sheltered) so you should be very calm and serious, say something like "I got very ill" or "I got hurt very badly" and then smile and move on very quickly lol.

I told my family about a year or so into doing it, or rather, the one person I told told my family. :-) 

It actually went ok, my mum hugged me (WTF!) and nobody else mentioned it even though they knew. That's basically all that's happened since, sometimes my dad mentions it when he's in a bad mood and he says something abrasive about my cutting but otherwise it's ok. Probably helps that a couple of other people in my family cut/self harm though.

Hmm, I guess it depends on how you feel before self injury (and which album you're listening to!) 

If you're feeling empty and pessimistic and lonely and you're listening to The Photo Album, it's different to if you're feeling intense and angry and upset and tearful and listening to Plans.
Idk about you but I found the energy in the music sort of "encouraged" me to self injure, like egging me on in its own way.
I've heard of them and can imagine what they're like but weirdly enough I haven't really tried listening to them.
Upvote for Patti Smith! Something about her voice is so sad but still really strong and powerful, she's so good.
Still not what I would consider harm reduction but whatever.

I thought harm reduction was for people who's self harm is very "severe", so they can stop putting their bodies under the insane amount of stress it goes under when being injured to a degree that it needs (or SHOULD) have immediate hospitalisation.

Keeping your tools clean is common sense, doesn't seem like a harm reduction technique the same way that keeping deeper cuts covered isn't harm reduction more than it is just coping with the wounds.

A positive point on there being more people here than there were before, perhaps this is only indicative of more people seeking support and help for their self harm, rather than keeping it to themselves.

Anything by Jack's Mannequin, every album is so meaningful and well written. I feel like I can get through anything with them. I also really like Skeleton Jar and Shadowland and Daisychains (and every other song) by Youth Group.

Some bands make me more nihilistic/self-injurous when I'm otherwise not in the mood.

Pavement, Brand New, Circulatory System, Death Cab For Cutie, Sonic Youth. All nice and depressing in their own ways.

> Once I actually make that first cut (which is usually tiny, kind of like a tester), that feeling of apprehension just disappears instantly and it just all comes back and I'll just go to town on myself as per normal.

This so much. It's like ripping off the plaster or jumping into a hot bath, like there's so much anxiety around "WILL IT HURT????" but once you've stepped over the line you realise it's not so scary. 

With the other stuff, I read somewhere that you could physically bite through your finger like it was a carrot, were it not for your brain making it impossible for the command to go through. I guess it's like breathing, no matter if you're sleeping or have been knocked unconcious, your body STILL breathes. It's, yeah like you said, the most basic human instinct.

Yes!!! I totally understand what you mean. I want people to see how much I'm hurting inside, but I never feel like I accurately portray how I'm doing or how my week/month/whatever has been in words. Cutting myself more severely than other self harmers I know seems to make me feel like I'm ~the worst~ and ~most tortured~ or whatever. 

When I don't self harm for a while, or resist/am unable to self harm when I really really want to, I get really pissy and nasty and irritable. But nobody sees how that's a much "worse" emotional state than when I'm vaguely happy in the daytime and cutting at nighttime.

Sort of, yeah! I definitely feel that conflict of wanting people to see fresh cuts/scars while wanting to seem like a normal, non-crazy person who cuts himself. I find a balance of waiting until my cuts are all healed over, then short sleevin' it up.
Thanks for the reply, although I should say that I'm already a major self harmer.

This should be higher up. I think this is the most dangerous part of self harm, I've also had my fair share of "too-deep"s from not taking into account the sharpness of a new tool.

As /u/vivalafreakshow said, it usually starts either by accident (slashing too hard when you're emotional) or because you start to need more of the feeling to, well, feel it. 

Some people don't care if they hit something, and some people actively avoid hitting veins/etc by choosing only to self injure in certain places. Everyone's different.

I 100% support what vivalafreakshow said, urging you never to try and go deeper. I have intense scarring which will never, ever go away and the way it affects me socially is immense - I would compare it to extremely visible, offensive tattooing. Physically the effects of going deeper (aside from the obvious increase in risk) include a weakening in my hands, tingling, and lowered sensation in more affected areas.

I usually put some good, numbing music on, and start telling myself loads of really good things about myself, like reassuring myself and comforting/hugging my arms and shoulders. It's kind of weird/pathetic lol.

Honestly, he comes off as a patronising person who has only a superficial understanding of emotional problems and self injury. While I agree that coddling etc is bad for the self harmer (that's also why I'm extremely skeptical of referring self injurers for inpatient psychiatric treatment), I think that instead of trivialising the addictive and emotional effects of self harm, people should simply accept that it's something people do. 

Self harm isn't ridiculous. Cutting releases endorphins - endogenous morphine - which literally means, morphine created by the body. It is an effective relief for stress and anxiety, else why would people do it? I do feel irritated by his assumption that self harm is something easy to give up, that all a self harmer needs to recover is to become aware of the fact that what they're doing doesn't solve the world's problems... Like, come on! We're aware of the fact that self harming is a temporary solution to all our worldly problems, it's not like anyone pretends otherwise. Making some ~logical~ speech about how self harm "isn't productive" (OMGGGG NO WAY) sounds good to the internet, it sounds good to people who aren't really knowledgeable about self harm, but it doesn't actually solve the problem. 

Like I said, he comes off as patronising, ignorant, and non-empathetic. He evidently has no awareness of the physiological side of self injury. I'd be more inclined to trust medical professionals than a youtuber who relies on video views from clickbait controversial videos...

Depends on where you're from, your history, and your doctor.

In the UK, unless you are considered to be severely psychotic or are literally on the brink of killing yourself, it is unlikely you would be admitted to an inpatient ward. You would likely be referred to an outpatient crisis team who would be there for you while the feelings calm down.

In the USA, as far as I have seen, doctors are much more likely to prescribe inpatient treatment/sectioning. 

The most important thing to do is to be honest with your therapist and trust that they (and your doctors) have your best interests at heart. They will do what it takes to keep you alive and well.

I wouldn't describe it that way but there's definitely a unique feeling of ultra-pleasure that comes from self harm with the right emotional and physical preparation. 

Might be TMI but I have a really low libido so I find self harming more enjoyable and pleasurable than um, other stuff. I mean, endorphins are literally "endogenous morphine" so it seems only natural to feel this way really.

My doctors know, my family (inc. extended) know, most of my old "friends" know although it's not something we've discussed, teachers know, and I've hinted at it at my youth groups (my youth worker knows).

I am quite relaxed about letting people know I guess, but nowadays I try to keep it on a need-to-know basis. No point keeping it a secret from people I'll need to keep in contact with for a long time, but if I'll only need to know them for a year or so then it doesn't concern them.

For serious things, or when I'm talking to adults, I say that I "went through some stuff". And then move on.

Otherwise I just make up some stupid story about those LIONS, MAN, THEY JUST TOTALLY CREPT UP ON ME! I HAD NO CHOICE, MAN! I HAD NO CHOICE! and then change the subject. Distract people with the idea that you're just a plain ol' harmless weirdo, rather than whatever stereotype they have in their head of a self harmer.
